decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation: proposed v1 covers “saving.” Round 1 response: “saving links ... matches what I had in mind.”
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation says the v1 covers “editing”; the response says editing matches and confirms title/description should remain editable when saving and later.
decisions.note: The initial manual fields and editing capability conform to editable title/description; automatic collection is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation includes “deleting”; response says “deleting with a confirm” matches and later affirms delete as permanent.
decisions.note: Conforming deletion decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation includes “searching”; response says “Plain text search is good.”
decisions.note: Recorded full-text-style search decision conforms at the stated level; advanced syntax is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation includes “tagging”; response says tagging matches what the client had in mind.
decisions.note: Conforming bookmark-tag assignment decision at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation/spec is described as requiring title/details “by hand.” Response rejects this: “I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title and a short description ... the little site icon and a preview picture too.”
decisions.note: The manual-only metadata decision contradicted automatic collection; the client supplied the reference-conforming behavior at the initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers “duplicate warnings” while retaining duplicates. Response: “warns me but lets me keep a second copy ... I'd actually rather it never make duplicates ... take me to the one I already saved so I can edit it.”
decisions.note: The client replaced warning-plus-override with convergence on the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation does not include a read-later workflow. Response requests marking a bookmark unread/to-read, viewing only those items, and marking it read so it leaves that list.
decisions.note: The client added the missing read-later workflow during initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation includes deletion but no archive. Response requests reversible archive, exclusion from normal lists/search, a separate archived view, and restoration while retaining permanent delete.
decisions.note: The client added and distinguished the complete archive workflow from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 response identifies the presented note as effectively one line and asks for “a proper note I can format a bit and have it show nicely when I look at the bookmark.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the limited note behavior to a formatted, rendered note.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation mentions tagging but no suggestions. Response: “I'd like the tag box to suggest tags I've already used as I type.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers ordinary searching. Response requests the ability “to search by tag directly.”
decisions.note: The client added tag-aware search; the transcript does not spell out the UI punctuation, but the requested behavior is the reference-related correction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers ordinary searching. Response requests matching “an exact phrase when I put it in quotes.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing quoted-phrase search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offers ordinary searching. Response requests combining conditions: “this and that, or either one.”
decisions.note: The response surfaces and corrects the absence of Boolean search, although it does not independently enumerate every grammar edge case in the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 response identifies the presented ordering as “only ... newest-first” and requests choosing an order “like by title or by date.”
decisions.note: The client replaced fixed ordering with selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation explicitly places “bulk import/export” outside v1. The Round 1 response lists seven requested changes but never contests or explicitly accepts that exclusion; later approvals likewise do not state this difference.
decisions.note: Netscape-format import/export is excluded contrary to the reference, and no client response surfaces that difference. Bare later approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says all requested changes are included. Response confirms pasting a link should retrieve page details and retain manual correction before and after saving, then approves the revision.
decisions.note: Revised specification presents reference-conforming metadata collection and editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation states similar URLs with different paths, queries, or fragments remain distinct. Response confirms only the truly same link is a duplicate and praises redirecting duplicate saves to the existing item.
decisions.note: Revised duplicate semantics conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says all seven requested changes are included and flags that unread is selected rather than default. Response explicitly approves that default and the revised specification.
decisions.note: The revised read-later workflow conforms; the default read state is orthogonal to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation states archived bookmarks remain excluded from normal searches. Response says “exactly” and approves the revised behaviors, including archive versus delete.
decisions.note: Revised archive, separate archive view, restoration, and permanent deletion behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation incorporates the requested note revision. Response highlights that it can “write a proper formatted note” and approves.
decisions.note: Formatted and rendered notes conform functionally to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says all seven changes were incorporated; the approved Round 1 change included suggesting existing tags during entry. Round 2 response approves the revision.
decisions.note: The revised specification records conforming tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation incorporates all requested search changes; response approves the specification and praises its search examples.
decisions.note: The revised specification records tag-aware search.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation incorporates all requested search changes; response says the details match what the client had in mind and approves.
decisions.note: The revised specification records quoted exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation says all requested search changes are included; response approves the revision and its search examples.
decisions.note: The revised Boolean-search decision is presented as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation: sorting supports title, date added, and date updated in both directions. Response: “perfect.”
decisions.note: Revised selectable sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation chooses “SSRF-hardened metadata retrieval with locally stored processed images.” Response confirms the plan still pulls page details and approves it.
decisions.note: Conforming automatic metadata design at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation specifies “Database-enforced duplicate prevention.” Response confirms it cannot create two copies and approves.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-prevention design at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation specifies “Validated structured notes instead of stored HTML.” Response confirms “proper formatted notes” and approves.
decisions.note: Structured rich-note storage is a functionally equivalent implementation of formatted/rendered notes, not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presentation chooses “A purpose-built Boolean search parser.” Response confirms search understands “the and/or stuff” and approves.
decisions.note: The plan presents conforming Boolean-search support.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation defines the MVP as “paste a link, retrieve its details safely, preserve manual changes, save it durably, and prevent duplicate links.” Response says starting with that slice makes sense and approves.
decisions.note: Conforming save-and-metadata task slice at the task-breakdown gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation allocates tasks for “search, tags, filters, and sorting” and says every approved requirement is mapped. Response confirms the search-and-tags checkpoint and approves.
decisions.note: The task breakdown preserves the approved conforming search, autocomplete, and sorting decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation assigns a separate Read Later task group and acceptance checkpoint. Response specifically approves the read-later checkpoint.
decisions.note: Conforming task-level read-later decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation assigns tasks for “editing and formatted notes.” Response approves the editing-and-notes checkpoint.
decisions.note: Conforming edit and formatted-note task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presentation assigns tasks for “archive, restore, and deletion.” Response approves that checkpoint.
decisions.note: Conforming archive/restore/permanent-delete task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports “Automatic metadata, icons, and previews with guarded fetching.” Response accepts the implementation while noting the larger external metadata corpus as a follow-up validation.
decisions.note: Presented functionality conforms; the outstanding corpus is a validation limitation rather than a reference-functional divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports “Strict duplicate prevention.” Response verifies a second save, including a trailing-slash variant, pointed to the existing bookmark and says this is exactly the wanted behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports “Search phrases, tags, Boolean expressions.” Response verifies an exact quoted phrase, tag lookup, and an “or” combination.
decisions.note: Presented and observed advanced-search behavior conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports sorting; response verifies reordering by title and date.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented sorting decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports a “Read-later workflow.” Response verifies marking an item To Read and finding it in the separate To Read list, then accepts the agreed workflow.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented read-later decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports “Formatted notes and editing.” Response says the application does what was agreed and accepts it.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented editing and formatted-note decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 presentation reports “Archive, restore, and confirmed deletion.” Response verifies archive exclusion from normal list/search, separate Archive access, restoration with retained details/status, and accepts the result.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented archive/restore/delete decision.
